name: MonarchDisclosureGroupStyle
title: Collapsible
summary: The Monarch look for the standard DisclosureGroup: a label with a chevron that shows and hides the content below it.
whenToUse: For one section that people open when they need it: advanced settings, details, evidence.
whenNotToUse: Inside a List or Form the system disclosure style usually fits better. Do not hide content that most people need.
api: init(expandedLabel: String? = nil, collapsedLabel: String? = nil)

states.name: collapsed
states.description: Only the header is shown; the chevron points down.

states.name: expanded
states.description: The content is shown under the header and the chevron points up.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The label and the chevron use the disabled text colour and the header does not respond, set with disabled(_:).

appearance: The label uses the default text colour in the label type role and the chevron the muted text colour; both use the disabled text colour when disabled. There is no border or fill, in every theme.
platformNotes: The web Collapsible has separate trigger and content parts, an optional chevron and an asChild trigger; Android ships MonarchCollapsible. On iOS the standard DisclosureGroup is the control, so Monarch ships only the style, the chevron is always shown, and the label is whatever the DisclosureGroup is given. The web keeps closed content mounted; SwiftUI removes it, so state inside the content is lost unless the app holds it.
accessibility: The header is one button; its label is the label of the group and its value is "Expanded" or "Collapsed".
Collapsed content is removed, so VoiceOver does not reach it.
The header is at least 44 points high and the whole row responds to touch.
The content appears without animation when Reduce Motion is on.
edgeCases: A long label wraps before the chevron.
State held inside the content is lost when the group collapses.
The expanded state is spoken as a value, because SwiftUI has no public expanded trait. This was not checked with VoiceOver on a device.
